# FEVER IN AN ASPLENIC PATIENT

Patients with impaired splenic function are at risk for severe and overwhelming infection with encapsulated bacteria. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most common cause of fulminant sepsis in patients with impaired splenic function, followed by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis. Infection with Capnocytophaga species is possible in asplenic patients with anteceding scratches and animal bites, especially dog bites. Babesiosis is also more likely in asplenic patients exposed to tick bites.

If fever develops in an asplenic patient, immediate administration of an antimicrobial agent is indicated, because fever can be the initial manifestation of a fulminant infection and prompt administration of an antimicrobial agent may prevent the development of clinical sepsis.

Administration of antibiotics should not be delayed for performing diagnostic studies, including lumbar puncture.
